text:
Help me write a public comment. I run a charter fishing boat out of our harbor, and the state fish and wildlife commission is taking comment on cutting the daily summer flounder limit from 4 fish per angler to 2.

Facts:
- I've run my boat for 22 years. I take out about 160 trips a season at $900 a trip for up to 6 people.
- There are 11 charter boats in our harbor.
- In a survey our charter association ran, 41 of 70 past customers said they would book fewer trips if the limit drops to 2. 12 said they'd book the same number.
- The commission staff's report says the flounder stock is at 78% of its target and recommends the cut for 3 years.
- Charter boats land about 9% of the state's summer flounder. Private boats land about 80%.
- The last time the limit was cut, in 2016, my bookings dropped from 170 trips to 138 the next season and came back to 155 two years later.

I want to say this limit will put every charter boat in our harbor out of business. I get two minutes at the microphone.

Before I draft, a few questions. Your 2016 numbers matter to my first one. A commissioner can check them, and they show your bookings dropping about 19% and then mostly coming back. That doesn't fit "every boat goes out of business," so the comment needs either a reason things would go worse this time or a claim your own numbers support.

1. **Why would this time be worse than 2016?** Is it fuel, insurance, slip fees, or loans on boats that leave less margin than you had then? Did any harbor boats actually close after 2016? If you can show your costs, what's your rough break-even in trips per season?
2. **What would you ask the commission to do instead?** For example, 3 fish instead of 2, a shorter cut, a separate limit for charter boats, or a review after one year. Commissioners are more likely to act on a specific alternative than on a flat no.
3. **What do you say about the stock being at 78% of target?** That's their main reason for the cut. Do you dispute the science? Are you seeing something different on the water? Or do you accept it and argue that charters, at 9% of the catch, shouldn't pay as much for it as private boats at 80%?
4. **What's the rest of the harbor worth?** Crew jobs, tackle shops, motels and restaurants that depend on charter customers. Any numbers you have, even rough ones.
5. **Who's speaking and who's backing you?** Your name and boat name, whether you're speaking for the charter association or just yourself, and whether other captains will be in the room.
6. **Is there anything a commissioner could raise that would hurt you?** For example, a past violation, the association pushing for a different limit before, or the survey's other 17 answers that aren't accounted for.

If you don't know some of these, say so and I'll write without them.

1. I don't know my break-even and I don't know if any boats closed after 2016. What I do know is two other captains in our harbor told me they'd sell if bookings drop like they did in 2016. I can't say how many boats would close overall. I only know my own books. I still want this as strong as you can make it without saying anything false.

2. We'd take 3 fish, or a shorter season, instead of 2. I can also commit to giving staff my trip logs from 2016 on. The association can commit to testing a catch-reporting app with staff next season.

3. I don't dispute their numbers. I don't have an answer to them. Go with the 9% vs 80% argument.

4. Don't know.

5. Captain Ray Dunn, the Sea Lark. I don't know yet if other captains will be there.

6. About 70% of my trips for this season are already booked. Not sure if that hurts or helps. I don't know about the other 17 survey answers.

I've written this to fit two minutes. It doesn't say every boat will close, because you can't back that up and a commissioner who knows the 2016 recovery would catch it. It argues from what you do know: your own losses, the survey, and the two captains who say they'd sell.

<final_document>
Good evening, Commissioners. I'm Captain Ray Dunn. I've run the Sea Lark out of [harbor name] for 22 years, about 160 trips a season.

I'm not here to argue with your staff's science. If the stock is at 78% of target, it needs help. I'm asking you to get it there without breaking the charter boats that bring people to this coast.

Here's what the last cut did. In 2016 the limit came down. The next season my bookings fell from 170 trips to 138. That's 32 trips, close to $29,000 at today's rate, gone from one boat in one year. It took two years to get back to 155, and I've never gotten back to 170.

I expect the same this time. Our charter association asked 70 past customers. Forty-one said they'd book fewer trips at two fish. Only 12 said they'd book the same. Two captains in my harbor have told me that if they lose bookings like they did in 2016, they'll sell. I can't tell you how many of our 11 boats would close. I can tell you it won't be none.

Charter boats land about 9% of this state's summer flounder. Private boats land about 80%. Our share of what this cut saves is small. Our share of what it costs is not.

So we're asking for three fish, or a shorter season, instead of two. And we'll help you find out whether it works. I'll give your staff my trip logs from 2016 on. Our association will test a catch-reporting app with your staff next season.

Let us help fix this without carrying more of the cost than our share. Thank you.
</final_document>

Notes:

- **Length:** It's about 290 words, which takes roughly two minutes at a steady pace. Time yourself reading it out loud. If you run long, cut the sentence "I'm asking you to get it there without breaking…"
- **The $29,000 figure** is 32 trips at today's $900 rate. If you charged less in 2016, keep the "at today's rate" wording so nobody can say you inflated it.
- **I left out the 70% of trips already booked.** A commissioner could hear it as "he's doing fine." If you're asked, the answer that helps you is that those customers booked expecting four fish, and you don't yet know how many will cancel.
- **Be ready for questions about the survey.** Nobody has accounted for the other 17 answers, so if you're asked, say you'll get the full results from the association. Don't guess. Before the hearing, check whether you can say how the 70 customers were chosen.
- **If other captains come,** have them stand when you mention the 11 boats.
